Here is the way I see it, and this is my basic problem with socialized anything.

There is no way to opt out. What If I personally do not want to participate? What If I personally want to enter into agreements with any entity that will allow me to manage my own healthcare? What I if I do not feel the need to have someone else manage that aspect of my life for me?

The concept compels cooperation using the police power of the state. If you do not want to participate, they will fine you. If you still refuse to participate and do not pay the fine, they will compel you to appear in court. If you still refuse, they will show up with guns, place you under arrest and lock you up until you go to face the judge.

And I also believe the cost effectiveness for the individual is not really a good argument. If your out of pocket is $30 for meds under a socialized system and the meds you require are cost $150, where does the extra $120 come from? the cost of the meds do not change, only the out of pocket expenses for it, the remainder has to come from somewhere.

One final argument I have against it is that under that system, you become entitled to a piece of another persons time and expertise with regard to the medical industry professionals. I just do not think that the government should require that a person be able to lay claim to another persons time, expertise and experience.
